correctness.rationale: For every finite length, stationary in-tree polynomials concentrate mass at the entrance singleton. Exact balance yields \(\pi_r(z_2)=r^{-1}+O(r^{-2})\), while all other vacant-site-1 nonempty configurations have probability \(O(r^{-2})\). Empty-state balance \(\alpha\pi_r(\varnothing)=\beta\pi_r(z_L)\) distinguishes \(L=2\) from \(L\ge3\). Particle conservation yields the claimed current coefficient. The accompanying checker reports 353 finite/symbolic assertions; the all-length proof is analytic.

value.rationale: The strong-reset limit for the canonical finite open exclusion process shows that leading throughput is independent of length and extraction rate for every \(L\ge3\), while \(L=2\) exhibits a sharp additional extraction contribution. This is a structural singular-transport statement with clear physical motivation, not an arbitrary numerical example.
